items.name: Wall Push-Up
items.description: The most accessible push-up variation, building chest, shoulder and arm strength while standing.
items.setup: Stand an arm's length from a wall. Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than your shoulders.
steps: Step back a little so your body leans toward the wall in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, keeping the elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Pause briefly when your nose is close to the wall.
Push the wall away to straighten your arms.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower toward the wall and out as you push away.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag or stick out.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Dropping the head forward.
items.harder: Step your feet further from the wall, or progress to the Incline Push-Up.
cautions: Make sure your shoes or socks will not slip on the floor.

items.name: Incline Push-Up
items.description: A push-up with the hands on a raised, stable surface – a step between wall push-ups and floor push-ups.
items.setup: Place a sturdy chair against a wall so it cannot slide (a kitchen counter or sturdy table also works). Put your hands on the edge, slightly wider than shoulder-width, and walk your feet back into a straight-body plank.
steps: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your body straight.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the edge of the surface.
Keep your elbows about 45 degrees from your sides.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
items.breathing: Breathe in on the way down and out as you press up.
mistakes: Using a chair that can tip or slide.
Letting the hips sag.
Bending the arms only a little.
items.easier: Use a higher surface, such as a counter, so you are more upright.
items.harder: Use a lower surface, or progress to Knee Push-Ups and then full Push-Ups.
cautions: Always brace the chair against a wall, and never use a chair with wheels.

items.name: Knee Push-Up
items.description: A floor push-up from the knees that builds strength toward the full version.
items.setup: Kneel on a mat or folded towel. Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders and walk them forward until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
steps: Brace your core and keep your hips in line with your shoulders and knees.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Lower until your chest is a few centimetres from the floor, or as far as you can control.
Press back up to straight arms.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you press up.
mistakes: Bending at the hips so your bottom sticks up.
Kneeling directly under the hips instead of leaning forward.
Letting the head drop toward the floor.
items.easier: Go back to Incline Push-Ups, or lower only part of the way.
items.harder: Hold the bottom position for a second, or progress to full Push-Ups.
cautions: Pad your knees with a mat or folded towel.
Use fists or push-up handles if your wrists are uncomfortable.

items.name: Push-Up
items.description: The classic bodyweight upper-body exercise for the chest, shoulders and triceps, with a strong core challenge.
items.setup: Start in a high plank: hands slightly wider than your shoulders, arms straight, legs extended and feet together or hip-width apart.
steps: Brace your core and glutes so your body is one straight line.
Bend your elbows, angling them about 45 degrees from your body, and lower your chest toward the floor.
Stop when your chest is just above the floor or at the lowest point you can control.
Press the floor away to return to straight arms.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you push up.
mistakes: Sagging hips or a raised bottom.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Doing half-range repetitions.
items.easier: Do Knee Push-Ups or Incline Push-Ups.
items.harder: Slow the lowering to three seconds, or raise your feet on a low step.
cautions: Use fists or push-up handles if your wrists are uncomfortable.
Stop if you feel pain at the front of the shoulder.

items.name: Pike Push-Up
items.description: A push-up performed with the hips raised, shifting the work toward the shoulders.
items.setup: Start in an upside-down V shape: hands shoulder-width apart, hips high, legs as straight as is comfortable.
steps: Walk your feet a little closer to your hands so your hips stay high.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor just in front of your hands.
Keep your elbows angled back rather than flared out.
Press back up to straight arms.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you press.
mistakes: Letting the hips drop so it turns into a regular push-up.
Lowering too quickly toward the head.
Flaring the elbows wide.
items.easier: Bend your knees, reduce the range, or place your hands on a sturdy step so the angle is less steep.
items.harder: Raise your feet on a stable chair seat for a steeper angle.
cautions: Lower slowly, and stop well before your head reaches the floor if control is difficult.
Avoid this exercise if head-down positions make you dizzy.

items.name: Chair Triceps Dip
items.description: Uses a stable chair to work the backs of the arms with your own bodyweight.
items.setup: Place a sturdy chair against a wall. Sit on the front edge with your hands gripping the seat beside your hips, fingers forward. Slide your hips off the seat with knees bent and feet flat.
steps: Keep your back close to the chair and your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Bend your elbows straight back to lower your body a short distance.
Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or earlier if your shoulders feel strained.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you press up.
mistakes: Drifting forward, away from the chair.
Letting the shoulders roll forward or shrug up.
Lowering too deep.
items.easier: Keep your feet closer to the chair and use your legs to help.
items.harder: Straighten your legs, keeping your heels on the floor.
cautions: Use only a stable chair braced against a wall.
Skip this exercise if it causes pain at the front of the shoulder.

items.name: Prone Y Raise
items.description: A face-down arm raise that strengthens the upper back and supports good posture.
items.setup: Lie face down on a mat with your forehead resting on a folded towel. Stretch your arms overhead in a Y shape, thumbs pointing up.
steps: Gently draw your shoulder blades down and back.
Lift both arms a few centimetres off the floor, keeping them straight.
Hold for one to two seconds without lifting your head.
Lower your arms slowly.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
mistakes: Lifting the head and bending the neck back.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
Using momentum to swing the arms.
items.easier: Lift one arm at a time, or bend the elbows slightly.
items.harder: Hold each lift for three to five seconds.
cautions: Keep the lift small; this is a precise, gentle movement.

items.name: Reverse Snow Angel
items.description: Sweeps the arms from your hips to overhead while lying face down to strengthen the upper back and the backs of the shoulders.
items.setup: Lie face down with your forehead on a folded towel and your arms by your sides, palms facing down.
steps: Lift your hands and arms slightly off the floor.
Sweep your arms out wide and up toward your head in a slow arc, like making a snow angel.
Turn your palms as your arms pass shoulder height so the movement stays comfortable.
Reverse the arc back to your hips, keeping the arms lifted.
items.breathing: Breathe steadily, breathing out as the arms travel overhead.
mistakes: Lifting the chest and arching the lower back.
Rushing the arc.
Resting the arms on the floor in the middle of a repetition.
items.easier: Reduce the range and stop at shoulder height.
items.harder: Pause for two seconds in the overhead position.
cautions: Keep the range pain-free for your shoulders.

items.name: Band Pull-Apart
items.description: Pulls a resistance band apart in front of the chest to strengthen the upper back and the backs of the shoulders.
items.setup: Stand tall holding a light resistance band in front of your chest with straight arms, hands about shoulder-width apart.
steps: Squeeze your shoulder blades together and pull the band apart by moving your hands out to the sides.
Keep your arms nearly straight and at chest height.
Pause when the band reaches or nears your chest.
Return slowly to the start, keeping tension in the band.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you pull apart and in as you return.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders.
Bending the elbows to make it easier.
Letting the band snap back quickly.
items.easier: Move your hands further apart on the band, or use a lighter band.
items.harder: Move your hands closer together, or use a stronger band.
cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before use and keep it away from your face.

items.name: Seated Band Row
items.description: A seated rowing movement with a resistance band looped around the feet, working the back and arms.
items.setup: Sit on the floor with legs extended and knees slightly bent. Loop the middle of the band around the soles of your feet and hold one end in each hand.
steps: Sit tall with your chest lifted and shoulders down.
Pull the band toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
Straighten your arms slowly to return.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
mistakes: Leaning back to pull with the body.
Rounding the shoulders forward.
Letting the band slip off the feet.
items.easier: Use a lighter band, or hold the band further from your feet.
items.harder: Shorten the band or use a stronger one, and pause at the end of each pull.
cautions: Make sure the band is secure around your feet before you pull.

items.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
items.description: Rows a pair of dumbbells toward the hips from a hinged position to build back and arm strength.
items.setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent, and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is at roughly 45 degrees. Let the weights hang below your shoulders.
steps: Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Pull the dumbbells toward your hips, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the weights slowly until your arms are straight.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you row and in as you lower.
mistakes: Rounding the back.
Jerking the weights up with the body.
Shrugging instead of rowing.
items.easier: Use lighter weights, or support one hand on a chair and row one arm at a time.
items.harder: Pause for two seconds at the top of each row.
cautions: Keep your back flat. If the hinged position bothers your lower back, row one arm at a time with the other hand supported on a chair.

items.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
items.description: Presses dumbbells overhead to build shoulder and arm strength, standing or seated on a chair.
items.setup: Sit tall on a sturdy chair or stand with feet hip-width apart. Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward or toward each other.
steps: Brace your core and keep your ribs down.
Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are almost fully extended overhead.
Keep your head neutral and finish with the weights roughly above your shoulders.
Lower them slowly back to shoulder height.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you press and in as you lower.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to push the weights up.
Pressing the weights forward instead of up.
Knocking the dumbbells together at the top.
items.easier: Use lighter weights or press one arm at a time.
items.harder: Slow the lowering phase to three seconds.
cautions: Skip overhead pressing if it causes shoulder pain, and seek qualified advice.

items.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
items.description: A simple curl that strengthens the fronts of the upper arms.
items.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms by your sides and palms facing forward.
steps: Keep your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders by bending at the elbows.
Squeeze briefly at the top.
Lower the weights slowly until your arms are straight.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and in as you lower.
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight.
Letting the elbows drift forward.
Dropping the weights quickly.
items.easier: Use lighter weights or curl one arm at a time.
items.harder: Lower the weights over three seconds, or pause halfway up.
cautions: Choose a weight you can lift without swinging.
